claim_one_line: A SINGLE STATE IS NOT KEPT WHEN HISTORIES ARE COMPOSED: THE WEB SEAT'S SEALED CARD VERIFIED ON MAIN (P-761, P-767, P-744, P-766; data-free; a weave question answered with the record's thread instrument for the state; the seat's code not run; ties decided in integers): in B1857's instrument a history is single when one run attains the apex, and the height of a run is sqrt(tr^2 - 4)/(2c) with c an integer of the word's matrix, so a tie is an equality of integers. Of the 36 ordered composites of six single histories 18 are single and 18 are not: the 18 with the same departure have the apex exactly twice, the 18 with different departures once, at the run of 6, leading by 1.89 to 1.91. In each of the 18 a symmetry of the composite's own cyclic word exchanges the two departures and keeps LR's line modulo 5, built as an integer matrix: the rotation by half for the 6 squares (det +1), one reversal for the other 12 (det -1, inverting the history); SnapPy gives each bundle twice as many isometries as its word has symmetries. Of the 216 triples 165 are single, 45 have the apex twice and 6 three times, so a third factor can make a composite single again; on the 258 words the runs at the apex are exactly one orbit of the word's symmetries; outside the family ties with no symmetry exist (16 of the 15641 cyclic run sequences to 18 letters). So 'single' is a property of one history's own cycle of heights and not a rule on what is allowed, and under the joint action of B1872 the first back-edge's admission condition does not define a set of allowed histories; whether it is kept as a labelled selection on one thread or replaced by a read-out on the whole, which needs a state of the whole and has none on record, is not decided here. Main adds a brute-force control over all primitive classes that one height per run is enough. 0 of 19.
